Players attempt to partition it into districts, place buildings, and construct canals. Districts are formed by completely surrounding areas of the island with water and then placing a District marker. The player who founds a district scores points immediately. In the scoring phases of the game, players score points based upon their dominance in each District. Spiritual Grandeur at the end of each Period Setup To start off, each player picks a spot in the Emperor's Palace to place their Pilli Mexica The Two Periods The game is played over 2 Periods If the 8 Calpulli tokens have been used to found Districts and one player has placed all 9 of their initial temples then period 1 ends when the round is complete and a scoring opportunity occurs Period 2 commences by granting each player 9 new temples regardless of how many they currently hold Period 2 ends the same way as 1, with using up the Calpulli and at least one player using all their temples Turn Each turn, a player has 6 Action Points to spend, different actions may cost variable amount of points, the actions and related cost are: Construct a Canal (1AP) Found a District (0AP) Construct or Move a Bridge (1AP) Build a Temple (1-4AP) Move your Pilla Mexica (1-5AP) Take an Action Point token (1AP) Spend an Action Point token (0AP) Construct a Canal You do not need to be adjacent to where you wish to build a canal It costs 1AP to place a Canal tile regardless of whether it is a single or double tile Canals are how you form districts, by blocking off areas, both orthogonal and diagonal adjacency forms a barrier A district can be made smaller later, however protected districts can no longer have their size amended (see Found a District) Found a District You have to be in the district you wish to found There needs to be an available Calpulli token which corresponds to the size of the district in squares (the big number on the upper portion) Construct or Move a Bridge You do not need to be adjacent to a bridge or the location where you wish to construct one Both sides of a bridge must be adjacent to land To relocate a bridge, all bridges must already be out and no pieces can be on the bridge you wish to move Build a Temple The cost of this action is equal to the size of the temple you wish to build i.e. the size 1 costs 1AP, whilst the size 3 costs 3AP You must be in the district you wish to build a temple The district does NOT need to be founded A Temple can only be built on an unoccupied land space A Temple can block a bridge or another piece (as long as said piece has the option of building a bridge to escape) Move your Pilla Mexica Other pieces, Temples, and Calpulli tokens are obstacles which stop movement To move one land space orthogonally is 1AP If your piece is on a bridge, you can move to any other bridge connected to it via water for 1AP, this water can be either a canal or the ocean (which borders the map) Bridges and pieces on bridges do NOT block bridge to bridge connections, assume you travel under the bridge via the water beneath it (however, you cannot land on an occupied bridge) For 5AP, you can move to any land space regardless of how it can be reached and what obstacles might be in the way Take an Action Point Token You can only take this action twice per turn at most You can only take a token if there is one in the supply [Rating: 1/10] The scoring doesn't do that much for me, and in hindsight the theme doesn't make that much sense. It becomes a bog standard area-majority race, only now there’s objects standing in the way of moving anywhere. But I really loved how players move [i]through[/i] the city, it felt like it came to life just from that alone.  It feels like it desperately needs a redesign, the objectives work fine but they’re the most boring in the world (bland even back when this came out). Once players are done with the freeform building, it’s noticeable how much the energy level drops, because it just won’t end un

[Rating: 2/10] game with many options. But I am not feeling like builder of pyramids. It is too much abstract for me, because I love games where theme is supported through mechanics.

[Rating: 2/10] Played this again to see if my years of additional gaming experience since my first run in with this game would change how little I enjoy it. Still much too open and much too political for my liking. Encourages lots of AP and it feels like the player who gets least punished by other players is the one to win, not the one who "played the best". In other words, everyone at the table decides the winner moreso than the winner themselves.

[Rating: 3/10] Massively overrated. Weak theme, unattractive pieces, limited strategies and serious turn-order inbalances.

[Rating: 3/10] The rules just plain don't make sense. This might change after I get to play it again, but no rush atm. :(

[Rating: 3/10] A couple of issues.  First is that the game can end if the supply of canal tiles runs out. If someone gets a good lead then they can easily just spend entire turns grouping a bunch of canal tiles into a section in order to end the game.  Another thing is that the game needs exactly four players. With three players, two players fighting for different spots can easily hand the game to the other player. This might get better with more experience, but the game wasn't good enough for me to want to explore it further.  Sold.

[Rating: 3/10] Interesting idea for area control but I feel that with 4 players turn order puts first and second players at a disadvantage especially as there is no change in the turn order for the second phase.

[Rating: 3/10] It looks really cool, but it's so confusing, we couldn't figure out where to start.

[Rating: 3/10] Area control game where people can stave off the end of a round a bit too long to my liking.

[Rating: 3/10] Ok area control/- dividing game. I'm not terribly fond of the end of the round(s) though. Just very few real surprises and upsets.
